messages:
sre-bot: [ALERT] PROD router: high tail latency detected — service=router-prod-usw2, metric=p99_request_duration, value=3200ms, threshold=500ms. Auto-page to #incidents and pinging oncall.

amy (oncall): acked. seeing p95 jump around 08:12 UTC. p95 ~1.4s (normal ~120ms), p99 ~3.2s. Streaming stalls reported by customers, partial degradations (no 5xx). Rolling window shows spike started ~07:58 UTC.

matt (observability): adding quick queries — prometheus: 
```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(router_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
```
returns ~3.2 -> corroborates alert. Per-shard breakdown: shard=47 showing 8x traffic vs baseline; region=us-west-2 showing ~65% of slow traces.

nina (sre): also seeing increased connection queue backpressure on router-47 (long accept latencies). Streaming connections show many stalled frames, tail CPU on router-47 is normal, but egress peers show hot fanout to a small set of model-serving hosts.

jamal (eng-runtime): any recent config changes? I see path-splitter rollout v2 at 07:55 UTC (traffic routing policy change: prefer-local->split-by-weight with sticky affinity). Could be mis-assigning hot prefixes to single shard.

amy (oncall): that would match the hot-partition symptom. quick customer-impact: support reports 4 paying customers with noticeable tail latency on streaming endpoints (low error rates, but high stall and perceived slowness). Notifying CSMs.

support (ops): posting interim note to affected customers: "We're investigating intermittent streaming lag; no data loss; mitigation in progress."

jamal (eng-runtime): triage plan: 1) check routing table diffs, 2) temporarily pause path-splitter-v2 rollout (rollback to v1), 3) shift traffic weights away from shard-47, 4) enable eager-fallback to smaller model variant for streaming requests if latency > 1s.

amy (oncall): agree. doing (2) now. matt — can you confirm how many prefixes are pinned to shard-47?

matt (observability): pulling prefix heatmap... 
```
Top prefixes -> shard-47: 42% of prefixes in last 10m (baseline 6%).
Hot keys: user:{uid:1234}, chat:{stream:abcd}
```

nina (sre): looks like affinity sticky cookie was inadvertently keeping traffic pinned after the split policy changed weights. Policy bug suggestion: when split weight < 20%, stickiness was not invalidated. That would create a persistent hot partition.

jamal (eng-runtime): ran `kubectl get configmap router-policy -o yaml` and noticed the new policy block with weights: 
```
path-splitter-v2:
  rules:
    - match: /chat/*
      weights:
        shard-47: 0.6
        shard-12: 0.3
        fallback: 0.1
  sticky: true
```
That 60% on shard-47 is too big for our normal distribution. Looks like a bad default.

amy (oncall): deploy-bot — please initiate rollback of path-splitter-v2. Tagging @jamal to lead.

deploy-bot: rollback initiated for config path-splitter-v2 -> target: path-splitter-v1. Action ID 8a3f. Estimated finish ~45s.

matt (observability): starting continuous query for p95/p99. updating dashboard.

nina (sre): while rollback runs, propose we also proactively redistribute prefixes away from shard-47 to avoid churn when rollback completes. Can we weight-down shard-47 by 50% at the LB level?

jamal (eng-runtime): yes. running `routerctl adjust-weight --shard=47 --factor=0.5` now.

amy (oncall): executing customer mitigation sequence: 1) rollback in flight, 2) weight adjust applied, 3) enable eager-fallback rule for streaming > 1s. I'll monitor user experience.

support (ops): updated status page: "Investigating increased tail latency in US-WEST-2, mitigations deployed."

matt (observability): rollback completed at 08:21 UTC. immediate p95 dropped from 1.4s -> 360ms within ~60s; p99 now ~580ms and trending down.

nina (sre): weight adjust looks effective. shard-47 traffic normalized. we still have some residual stalls — likely KV cache warmup & connection draining.

jamal (eng-runtime): enabling eager-fallback for streaming routes older than 1s now — rule applied. Expect small quality tradeoff but big latency improvement.

amy (oncall): handing oncall to jamal for next 45 minutes while I start incident writeup. jamal — please verify no regressions and confirm recovery.

jamal (eng-runtime): ack. I'll own post-mitigation scrub. Initial customer-impact: 4 customers saw degraded streaming for ~20-28 minutes. No data loss, no 5xx. We'll prepare an RCA with timeline and root cause (routing policy misconfig + sticky affinity bug).

matt (observability): grabbing logs for root cause analysis. snapshots: request traces show long queue_time before route selection for affected requests; many traces show same prefix pinned to same backend.

nina (sre): action items for incident doc: (1) RCA with config diff and sticky invalidation bug, (2) revert-to-default gating for path-splitter rollouts (automated canary check), (3) add telemetry to detect prefix concentration (heatmap alert), (4) fix policy codepath to invalidate stickiness on weight changes.

amy (oncall): adding to incident ticket and tagging eng-runtime + eng-sre + product for prioritization. I'll include list of impacted customers for CS.

support (ops): confirming CS notified. template note: "We've reverted a routing change that caused uneven traffic concentration; performance should be back to normal. We'll follow up with a detailed RCA."

jamal (eng-runtime): current metrics at 08:28 UTC: p95 190ms, p99 320ms. Closing the live mitigation portion. Scheduling a follow-up meeting in 2 hours to review RCA drafts and remediation timeline.

sre-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> watchers stay subscribed for RCA. Assigning incident-id INC-2026-0937.

amy (oncall): closing handoff. thanks team. :thumbsup:
